# The tdd record cannot be written, and the reason is a gap SEEN-113 left

All four slices are proved. 1,521 harness tests pass, `doctor` is clean with no
problems and no warnings, `rules --check` reports 22 rules and nothing
untraceable, coverage on `packages/core` is 100.0 with a delta of 0.0, and the
regression is record 49. The work is done. The journal cannot say so.

## What the gate refuses, exactly

    The tree moved under check 14: it ran against 93017c2ee4a3 and this record is
    written against 1ed812a5aa3a, compared over the whole tree because no
    accepted tdd record says which slice of the plan check 14 proved, so the
    position this record names for it is corroborated by nothing but itself. Its
    evidence is about code this ticket has changed since, so it does not support a
    citation here; run it again in this attempt

The ordering is fine: slice 1 cites 12 and 14, slice 2 cites 23 and 28, slice 3
cites 34 and 35, slice 4 cites 41 and 48, and the regression at 49 is last. Each
red precedes its green, the ranges do not overlap, and each pair is within one
attempt. The one thing wrong is that slices 1 to 3 were proved in attempt 2 and
this record is written in attempt 3, after the return at record 37.

## Why SEEN-113's mechanism does not reach it

SEEN-113 exists for exactly this: a tdd record citing evidence a return did not
invalidate. Its mechanism scopes the tree comparison to the files the cited
check's slice names, because the whole tree can never answer the question on a
ticket whose later slices added code. That scoping is granted on one condition,
at `harness/gates.py` around line 703: `if not declared`, meaning no **accepted**
tdd record says which slice the cited check proved, the comparison falls back to
the whole tree and the citation is refused.

A ticket that returns to solution before it has ever advanced out of tdd has no
accepted tdd record. So every citation it makes across the return falls back to
the whole tree, and the whole tree has moved by definition, because the slices
after the return wrote code. The condition SEEN-113's repair depends on is one
this shape of ticket cannot satisfy, and the refusal it gives is the one SEEN-113
was written to stop.

It is a narrow gap and a reproducible one: prove a slice, return to solution,
prove another slice, try to write the record. It is not a disagreement with
SEEN-113's reasoning, which is right about self-corroboration being worthless
(F1 of its third review). It is that the first accepted record has to come from
somewhere.

## Why the two obvious ways out are not ways out

**Re-running the greens now** puts them after the regression at record 49, and the
ordering rule requires `green <= regression`. Measured: record 51 is
`./scripts/rules.sh fixtures` green in attempt 3, and citing it for slice 1 is
refused with "Slice 1 is out of order".

**Re-running the reds now** cannot work on its own, because a red is a test that
fails and these tests pass: the code that makes them pass is in the branch.

## The two that are

**Replay the whole sequence in attempt 3.** For each slice in order, check the
tree back to the commit before that slice, run the slice's red command and record
it, check the slice's commit back in, run it again and record the green. Then one
fresh regression last. Eight checks and a seven-minute regression, and the reds
are genuine: the same commands against the same trees, failing for the same
reasons, which is what the gate asks for when it says to run them again. What it
costs is a journal whose reds for slices 1 to 3 were recorded hours after the code
existed, and a reader has only this note to tell them why.

**Fix the gap in a harness ticket of its own, and let this ticket wait.** The
repair is in `harness/gates.py`, which this ticket has already changed in slice 3,
and that is the argument against doing it here: a ticket amending the gate it must
itself pass, in order to pass it, is the worst shape a review can be handed. A
separate ticket also gets the question the repair really turns on, which is where
the first corroboration comes from when there is no accepted record, decided on
its own evidence rather than under the pressure of unblocking something.

Recorded before either is chosen, because the choice is Ruud's and the facts
should not have to be reconstructed from a transcript afterwards.
